content.value_statement: Medical device companies need expert guidance for EU market compliance under MDR 2017/745. This skill provides comprehensive tools for classification decisions, technical file preparation, clinical evidence requirements, and post-market surveillance implementation.
actual_capabilities: Provides expert guidance on MDR classification under Annex VIII
Ensures comprehensive technical file preparation meeting Annex II and III requirements
Develops clinical evidence strategies including literature review and clinical investigations
Implements post-market surveillance systems meeting MDR Chapter VII requirements
Guides benefit-risk analysis and GSPR compliance
Supports UDI system implementation and EUDAMED registration
Facilitates Notified Body interface and audit preparation
limitations: Does not replace formal Notified Body assessment
Regulatory requirements evolve; users should verify latest MDR guidance

output_examples.input: What is the MDR classification for my device?
output: MDR classification depends on: device duration (transient/short-term/permanent), invasiveness (non-invasive/invasive), body system affected, and specific rules in Annex VIII
Classes: I (low risk, self-certified), IIa (low-medium risk), IIb (medium-high risk), III (high risk, prior scrutiny)
Software classified per MDCG 2019-11 based on purpose and functioning

output_examples.input: What is required for MDR technical documentation?
output: MDR Technical File (Annex II) includes: Device description, Design and manufacturing information, GSPR checklist, Risk management, Clinical evaluation, PMCF plan, Labeling, Verification and validation
Must demonstrate compliance with General Safety and Performance Requirements (GSPR)

best_practices: Start MDR compliance planning early in product development
Engage Notified Body early for complex classification questions
Maintain comprehensive technical documentation throughout device lifecycle
Implement robust PMS system from market entry
Keep clinical evaluation current with new data
anti_patterns: Waiting until product launch to address MDR requirements
Copying technical files without understanding requirements
Failing to update clinical evaluation with new data
Neglecting PMS obligations after market entry

faq.question: What is the difference between MDD and MDR?
faq.answer: MDR (2017/745) has stricter requirements including: expanded device scope, stronger clinical evidence requirements, increased post-market surveillance, UDI requirements, and broader economic operator responsibilities.

faq.question: What is the MDR transition timeline?
faq.answer: MDR became applicable May 26, 2021. Certificates under MDD remain valid until expiration or May 2024 (with extensions). Class I devices self-certified under MDD could register under MDR from May 2021.

faq.question: What is GSPR?
faq.answer: General Safety and Performance Requirements - the essential requirements in Annex I that devices must meet to obtain CE marking under MDR.

faq.question: What is PMCF?
faq.answer: Post-Market Clinical Follow-up - ongoing activities to proactively collect clinical data after device market entry to confirm safety and performance.

faq.question: What is EUDAMED?
faq.answer: European Database on Medical Devices - electronic system for registration, coordination, and information sharing on medical devices in the EU.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. This tool provides regulatory guidance. Consult MDR-registered regulatory consultants or legal counsel for formal submissions.
